title: Values Seen Twice
statement:
An array nums of length n holds values from 1 to n. Every value appears once or twice, never more. Return every value that appears twice, in any order.

Aim for O(n) time and O(1) extra memory besides the output. You may change nums while you work.

examples.why: 3 and 1 each appear twice; 4 and 6 once; 2 and 5 never. [1, 3] is accepted too.

constraints: Each value appears at most twice
hints: With a set this is easy. What spare room does the input itself give you?
Every value v points to a slot, index v − 1. You can leave a mark in that slot without losing what was stored there.
Flip the sign of nums[v − 1] the first time you see v. If it is already negative when you arrive, v is a repeat. Use Math.abs when reading values.

explain.intuition:
Values run from 1 to n and the array has n slots, so each value owns one slot: v owns index v − 1. Use the sign of that slot as a "seen" flag. The number stored there keeps its size, so nothing is lost; you just read it with abs.

When you visit v and its slot is still positive, flip it negative. If it is already negative, someone flipped it before: v is the second copy. It is the same trick as storing a visited bit inside a data structure you already have, instead of allocating a separate map.
steps: Look at slot v − 1. If nums[v − 1] < 0, push v to the answer.
pitfalls: Reading nums[i] without abs after it was flipped, which gives a negative index.
Collecting the answer at the end from the negative slots. A negative slot only means its value was seen at least once; the repeat has to be caught at the moment you find the slot already negative.
Counting values that never appear as duplicates. Only a slot found already negative means a repeat.

solutions.title: Seen-set
solutions.idea: Keep a set of values seen so far; a value already in it is a repeat.

solutions.title: Sign marking in place
solutions.idea: Each value v owns slot v − 1. Flip that slot's sign on the first visit; a slot already negative means a second visit.

followups: Restore the array to its original values before returning. What does it cost?
Now find the values from 1 to n that never appear, with the same O(1) memory.
lcTitle: Find All Duplicates in an Array
